Object class is the superclass of all Java classes.
Every class in Java implicitly extends java.lang.Object.
Methods of the Object class are inherited by all classes and can be overridden.

sections.heading: Important Methods of the Object Class

rows: Returns the runtime class of an object.
Returns a hash code value for the object (used in hashing structures like HashMap).
Returns a string representation of the object.

items: By default, equals() compares memory addresses (similar to ==).
Can be overridden to perform content-based comparison according to business needs.
Generates a 32-bit integer hash code used in hash-based data structures like HashMap.
Default implementation uses memory address.
Should be overridden along with equals() for consistency.
If two objects are equal (equals() returns true), their hashCode() must be the same.
If two objects have the same hashCode(), they might or might not be equal.
Always override both methods together to maintain consistency.

content.text: Wrapper classes are used to represent primitive types (int, char, etc.) as objects.

items: Java Collections (like ArrayList, HashSet) can only store objects, not primitives.
Autoboxing: Automatic conversion of primitives to corresponding wrapper objects.
Unboxing: Automatic conversion of wrapper objects back to primitives.
Parse Methods: Convert a String into a primitive type (parseInt(), parseDouble(), etc.).
